content: Fall down seven times, stand up eight.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Nana korobi ya oki (七転び八起き) — Classical Kotowaza
explanation: Life inevitably brings defeat, unexpected setbacks, and grief. The classical Japanese concept of Nana Korobi Ya Oki teaches that nobility is not measured by avoiding failure, but by the relentless refusal to remain on the ground. The eighth rising is where true human dignity is forged.
practicalInsight: When disappointment strikes today, don't waste energy mourning the fall. Set your feet firmly on the earth and take the single next step.
reflectionPrompt: What recent stumble have you allowed to paralyze you, and what would your 'eighth rising' look like right now?
